learning_outcomes.text: The student will conduct an in-depth cultural analysis of the phenomena of counselling and coaching from the perspective of the history of ideas and social practices.
The student knows specialized terminology in the field of selected philosophical concepts, which is used in contemporary cultural practices related to counselling and coaching.
The student justifies the application value of philosophical theses in counselling and coaching.
The student performs a detailed analysis of philosophical text to prepare a theoretical basis for interpreting contemporary cultural phenomena related to counselling and coaching.
The student conducts Socratic dialogue in traditional and contemporary forms and understands the culture-forming function of such an event.

syllabus_topics: Comparison of classical philosophical wisdom and Socratic dialogue with contemporary counselling and coaching practices to understand how current culture replicates or modifies classical patterns, and their individual and general cultural consequences.
Coaching combined with practical philosophy as a means of reaching deep sources of human development, applicable personally and professionally.
Philosophy of life and ethics as a basis for philosophical counselling and coaching, stimulating personal and professional development, and building team, organizational, and corporate culture.
Philosophical counselling and coaching as methods to reach deep sources of human development across all dimensions and throughout life.
Philosophical consulting teaching methods to master skills, acquire information, knowledge, and above all, life wisdom for holistic and sustainable development without professional burnout.

The first National Philosophical Counseling Association in the US (1991) and the postulate for a return to practical philosophy, meaning a wise way of life leading to eudaimonia (happiness), drawing inspiration from Socratic dialogue and Stoic methods of controlling thoughts, emotions, and behavior.
Modern pragmatism, philosophy of life, analytical philosophy, and phenomenology as important sources.
Coaching understood as a set of methods for effectively implementing a chosen and defined philosophy of life, encompassing individual, professional, and social dimensions.
Philosophical way of thinking as a method of discovering the meaning of life.
Philosophical diagnosis: logical analysis of beliefs and their practical emotional, behavioral, interpersonal, and social consequences.
Socratic method as a way of discovering human creative potential.
The essence of Platonic dialogue: the art of asking questions and the creative experience of silence.
Knowledge is within man: Plato's path to wisdom. Plato's Academy as a model for organizations stimulating development.
Stoic rules of life practice.
Stoic methods of controlling thoughts, emotions, and behavior and engagement in social life.
Altruism as a way of self-realization and achieving a state of eudaimonia.
Coaching conversation – a new incarnation of Socratic dialogue.
Discovering values – the primary goal of coaching.
Understanding in building relationships that stimulate individual and team development.
Methods for improving different levels of dialogical listening.
Methods for practicing intuition.
Methods for improving the ability to ask development-stimulating questions. Developing emotional intelligence in a coaching relationship.
assessment_rules: To pass the course, students must have a minimum of 50% attendance at lectures and achieve a positive grade on the final written colloquium. The scope of the colloquium covers topics presented during classes.
